chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who becomes junub: is it sufficient for his ghusl of janabah that he stand in the rain until he washes his head and body, while he is able to do otherwise? He said: If he washes himself with it as he would perform his washing with water, that will suffice him.

So this report also admits the possibility that he only permitted it for him when he himself washes the limbs at the time the rain falls upon him, according to the order in which they must be arranged. It also admits the possibility that the position regarding it is what we said concerning the first report: that it is sequential in legal ruling, not in actual performance; or that this is a ruling specific to him, excluding one who intends ghusl by placing water upon his body.

key_terms.الْمَطَرِ: rain used here as the water source for ghusl
key_terms.تَرْتِيبُهَا: their required order or sequence in washing the limbs
key_terms.جَسَدَهُ: the body, whose washing completes the ghusl in this report
key_terms.رَأْسَهُ: the head, mentioned as a principal part to be washed
key_terms.غُسْلِ الْجَنَابَةِ: the ritual bath required after janabah
key_terms.لَا فِعْلًا: not sequential in actual outward performance

ai.seo_question: Is ghusl al-janabah valid by standing in the rain instead of pouring water directly on the body?
ai.summary: This report discusses whether ghusl al-janabah may be valid by standing in rainfall and washing the head and body with it. The closing discussion explains possible juridical understandings of the report, especially concerning the requirement of ترتيب in ghusl and whether the ruling is general or specific.
